Introduction and meaning
Procuration of child. BNS restatement of IPC 366A. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 366A. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 96 is the rule on “Procuration of child”. The section provides that whoever, by any means whatsoever, induces any child to go from any place or to do any act with intent that such child may be, or knowing that it is likely that such child will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 96 exists so that “Procuration of child” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 96 (Procuration of child), Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever, by any means whatsoever, induces any child to go from any place or to do any act with intent that such child may be, or knowing that it is likely that such child will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 96 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 96 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

learningObjectives: Master the elements of procuration of a child under BNS s. 96.
Analyze the actus reus: inducing a child to go from any place or perform any act.
Understand the mens rea: intent or knowledge that the child will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse.
Examine the statutory penalty of imprisonment up to ten years and fine.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 96 criminalizes whoever, by any means whatsoever, induces any child to go from any place or to do any act with intent that such child may be, or knowing that it is likely that such child will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person, punishable with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Criminalizes the procuration and trafficking of children for sexual exploitation by penalizing any inducement directed at facilitating non-marital sexual intercourse.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 96 (corresponding to IPC s. 366A).
Actus reus: Inducing any child by any means whatsoever to go from any place or do any act.
Target: Any child (under eighteen years of age).
Mens rea: Intent or knowledge that the child will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person.
Punishment: Imprisonment of either description extending up to ten years, and fine.
essentialIngredients: The victim is a child (under eighteen years of age).
The accused induced the child to go from any place or do any act.
The inducement was effected by any means whatsoever (persuasion, deceit, promises, or gifts).
The accused acted with intent or knowledge that the child will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 96 penalizes the procuration of minors. Under the old IPC (s. 366A), the provision applied to girls under eighteen years. Under BNS s. 96, the term used is 'child', encompassing any minor under eighteen years of age regardless of gender. The actus reus is broad: inducing the child 'by any means whatsoever' (deceitful promises of employment, gifts, or persuasion) to leave a place or perform any act. The specific mens rea required is the intention or knowledge that the child will be forced or seduced into illicit intercourse with a third party. The offence is complete upon the inducement with the requisite intent; actual intercourse is not necessary for liability under s. 96.
examples: Teaching example (Luring a minor with job promises): An accused approaches a 15-year-old child in a rural bus depot, promising a lucrative acting job in a metropolis, with the intent of delivering the child to a third party for sexual exploitation. The offence under s. 96 is complete upon inducing the child to travel.

Teaching example (Direct intercourse vs third party): A man induces a minor to go with him for his own sexual relations. This falls under kidnapping/rape provisions (ss. 137, 63); s. 96 specifically addresses procuration for illicit intercourse with 'another person'.
distinctions: Section 96 vs Section 98 (Selling child): Section 96 covers inducing a child to go or act for illicit intercourse; Section 98 specifically penalizes commercial transactions of selling, hiring, or disposing of a child for prostitution.

Section 96 vs Kidnapping (s. 137): Kidnapping requires taking or enticing out of the keeping of a lawful guardian; Section 96 focuses on inducing the child to go from any place with sexual procuration intent.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who persuaded a sixteen-year-old child to leave school and travel to another city knowing the child was to be handed over to a client for commercial sex is liable under s. 96.
Rule: Inducing a child to go from any place with knowledge that the child will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person constitutes an offence under BNS s. 96.
Application: The victim was under eighteen, inducement was proven, and the destination was sexual exploitation by a third party.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 96.

keyTakeaways: Applies to any child under eighteen years of age.
Criminalizes inducing a child by any means to leave a place or do an act.
Requires intent or knowledge that child will face illicit intercourse with another person.
Punishable with up to ten years imprisonment and fine.
